output.question: What are Whirlpool's subsidiaries?
output.answer: Whirlpool Corporation's latest subsidiary list is Exhibit 21 of its 10-K for fiscal 2025 (year ended Dec 31, 2025), which was filed with the SEC in 2026. It names 118 subsidiaries. The main groups are the KitchenAid entities (KitchenAid, Inc. in Ohio plus units in Europe, Asia, Australia and the UAE), the Maytag entities (Maytag Sales, Inc., Maytag Limited and others), and the InSinkErator entities (InSinkErator LLC plus units in Canada, the UK, Australia and China). Brazil's Whirlpool S.A. and Brasmotor Ltda. and Mexico's Industrias Acros Whirlpool are also on the list. So are holding and finance companies in Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Delaware and Nova Scotia, and smaller units such as Xpelair Ltd (UK), Haceb Whirlpool Industrias (Colombia), Whirlpool Insurance Company (Bermuda) and Whirlpool Asia LLP (India). Whirlpool of India Limited is not on the FY2025 list.

key_facts.fact: Whirlpool's FY2025 Exhibit 21 'List of Subsidiaries' names 118 entities.

caveats: The page I read shows no as-of date. It is the Exhibit 21 in the FY2025 10-K filing (accession 0000106640-26-000009), but I did not confirm the exact filing date.

The list may have changed after it was filed, through divestitures, mergers or new entities. Whirlpool cut its stake in Whirlpool of India during 2025, and that company does not appear on the FY2025 list.
Whirlpool owns part of Beko Europe, but Beko Europe is not a subsidiary, so it is not on the list.
Companies commonly leave out minor subsidiaries in Exhibit 21. The page I read has no note saying whether any were left out.
Brand names such as Amana, JennAir and Hotpoint can be brands rather than separate legal subsidiaries, so they may not show up under their own names.
